# Stripboard Editor

> A free online editor for designing circuits on stripboard (also called
> Veroboard). It pairs a schematic editor with a stripboard layout editor,
> and includes a router that can lay out the whole board automatically.

Stripboard is prototyping board made of a grid of holes over parallel
copper strips, where every hole on a strip is already electrically
connected. Building a circuit on it means placing components, cutting
strips to separate nets, and adding link wires to bridge connections a
strip cannot carry. Stripboard Editor supports doing this by hand or
handing it to an automatic router.

## Core features

- Schematic editor with a standard symbol library, wiring, and nets.
- Stripboard editor with live strip colouring that shows nets and conflicts
  in real time.
- Automatic layout router: places every component, sizes the board, and
  generates the strip cuts and link wires needed to complete it. It is
  deterministic, so the same circuit always produces the same layout.
- The router also tidies its own result: a second pass straightens link
  wires and keeps them from crossing over components, and the strip cuts
  are placed as drilled holes lined up in shared columns, the way a
  builder would make them.
- Per-component-type layout settings: the allowed pin-to-pin span for
  flexible parts (e.g. how many holes a resistor may stretch across), and
  the clearance kept around a part's body, down to 0 for placing parts
  directly side by side.
- Board size can be locked (fix rows and/or columns to fit a board you
  already own) and individual components can be locked in place before
  running the router, which will then design the rest of the layout
  around them.
- Manual board editing alongside the router: place cuts and link wires by
  hand, run wires in parallel on the same strip column, and insert or
  delete a board row or column at any position.
- Editable component footprints, and a custom component editor for parts
  outside the built-in library.
- Printable 1:1 build template: a component-side placement sheet, a
  mirrored copper-side cut sheet, and a bill of materials (BOM).
- KiCad-compatible netlist export, so a circuit prototyped here can move
  into a PCB tool. Most built-in parts map to real KiCad symbols and
  footprints.
- No account required to use or save a project; accounts add a project
  dashboard and shareable edit/view-only links.

## Pages

- [Quick guide](https://stripboard-editor.com/guide): keyboard shortcuts,
  workflow, and an overview of every feature above.
- [How auto-layout works](https://stripboard-editor.com/guide/auto-layout):
  a plain-language explanation of the router's stages and what you can
  configure.
- [What's new](https://stripboard-editor.com/updates): changelog and
  planned work.
